blockMcqs.question: What does an inverted index map?
options: Word to the documents that contain it
Document to the words it contains
Row ID to its byte offset on disk
Query to its cached result set
blockMcqs.explanation: It flips the natural document-to-words direction so lookups need no scanning.

blockMcqs.question: Why are posting lists kept sorted by doc ID?
options: To rank results by relevance score
To make boolean AND/OR cheap merges
To preserve document insertion order
To allow prefix lookups on terms
blockMcqs.explanation: Sorted lists let intersection and union run as a linear two-pointer pass.

blockMcqs.question: Why must index-time and query-time analyzers match?
options: To keep the term dictionary sorted
To balance shards evenly across nodes
Otherwise tokens differ and matches fail
To let BM25 compute IDF correctly
blockMcqs.explanation: Matching happens in token space; mismatched normalization returns zero hits.

blockMcqs.question: What two fixes does BM25 add over plain TF-IDF?
options: Stemming and synonym expansion
Sharding and replication
Phrase matching and fuzzy search
Term saturation and length normalization
blockMcqs.explanation: It flattens repeated-term gains and penalizes long documents; IDF stays.

blockMcqs.question: How does Lucene delete a document from a segment?
options: Rewrites the segment without that doc
Marks a tombstone, reclaims it at merge
Removes it instantly from the posting list
Decrements the shard's primary count
blockMcqs.explanation: Segments are immutable, so the space is freed only during background merges.

blockMcqs.question: Why is primary shard count fixed at index creation?
options: Replicas would otherwise outnumber primaries
The translog cannot grow afterward
Routing is hash(id) % primaries
Lucene segments would stop merging
blockMcqs.explanation: Changing the divisor re-buckets nearly every document, breaking existing postings.

blockMcqs.question: What does aggressive stemming and synonyms trade away?
options: Recall, in favor of precision
Precision, in favor of recall
Durability, in favor of throughput
Read latency, in favor of writes
blockMcqs.explanation: Looser matching finds more results but drags in irrelevant junk.

blockMcqs.question: What makes index-then-immediately-query tests flaky?
options: Shards rebalance on every write
BM25 recomputes IDF asynchronously
Replicas acknowledge before the primary
Docs are searchable only after a refresh
blockMcqs.explanation: A new doc is durable via translog but not visible until the next refresh.
